_doc: DOJ FCA and healthcare fraud settlements >= $25M for predictive detector. In-sample window: 2020-01-01 to 2024-12-31. Blind window: 2015-01-01 to 2018-12-31. Below-threshold (<$25M) settlements recorded but had_settlement=false for detector. Sources: DOJ press releases (justice.gov), HHS-OIG enforcement, news coverage.
search_methodology: WebSearch + WebFetch on DOJ press release archive and HHS-OIG enforcement, plus secondary sources (Becker's, Modern Healthcare, law firm summaries). Each obligor searched by name + 'False Claims Act' + date range. Negative findings (no settlement) recorded with confidence based on search coverage.

in_sample_period_2020_2024.note: No FCA settlement >$25M found in 2020-2024 for Adventist Health West (Roseville, CA). Distinct from Adventist Health System Sunbelt (FL/SE) which had the $115M 2015 Stark settlement.

West Penn Allegheny (predecessor) had $1.5M FCA settlement in 2015 from self-disclosure of lease/Stark issues. Below $25M threshold.
Tower Health was created 2017 from Reading Health acquisition; no FCA actions found.

blind_period_2015_2018.note: UC Health/West Chester Hospital paid $4.1M in 2015 for medically unnecessary spine surgeries (Durrani case). Below $25M threshold.

in_sample_period_2020_2024.note: $5.7M ERISA retiree benefits class settlement found, not FCA. No DOJ FCA settlement.

$3M Medicaid 60-day overpayment FCA settlement (predecessor entities). $5.3M HIPAA/Meta Pixel class action settlement (not FCA). Both below threshold.

blind_period_2015_2018.note: Beth Israel/St. Luke's/Continuum (now Mount Sinai entities) paid $2.95M in 2016 for delaying Medicaid overpayment repayment. Below threshold.

in_sample_period_2020_2024.note: Formerly Lifespan; rebranded Oct 2024. No FCA settlement found.

blind_period_2015_2018.note: Heartland Regional Medical Center (Mosaic predecessor) paid $5.5M in 2014 to settle FCA wage index/cost report case in MO (St. Joseph); predates blind window. Subsequent civil settlements were medical malpractice or debt collection class actions, not FCA.

in_sample_period_2020_2024.note: St. Peter's Health $10.8M settlement Aug 2024 is Helena, Montana, NOT Saint Peter's Healthcare System NJ. Different entity. NJ Saint Peter's: no FCA actions found.

Multiple small OIG Civil Monetary Penalties settlements ($57K-$442K) for unlicensed individuals submitting claims. None FCA, none above threshold. Tampa General Hospital is distinct from Moffitt Cancer Center ($19.5M clinical trial billing).
FLSA wage rounding suit pending; no FCA settlement found.

$3.3M Stark Law FCA settlement May 2025 - just outside in-sample window (which ends 12/31/2024). Below threshold anyway.

HHS ADA settlement re: deaf patients found, not FCA. No FCA action in blind window.

Eisenhower paid $8M FCA settlement in 2005 (cost report fraud) - well outside blind window. No new actions in 2015-2018.

Baptist Health Services CMP settlement $1.4M (date unclear) for office visit records - below threshold and not formal DOJ FCA.

No FCA settlement found specifically for Mercy Health Services Baltimore (Mercy Medical Center) in blind window. Note: MedStar Health $35M settlement was March 2019 (post-blind-window) and is a different obligor entirely.
Subsequent class actions re: Meta Pixel data sharing (2023+) not FCA. EEOC ADA settlement $375K not FCA. No FCA action in blind window.

Note: Bayhealth Milford (DE) — different entity — was part of multi-hospital kyphoplasty FCA settlement; Milford Regional MA: no FCA found.

Adventist HealthCare MD is a separate corporate entity. No FCA action found for the MD obligor.

blind_obligors_with_below_threshold_fca_: East Texas Medical Center/ETMC ($21M, Aug 2018, AKS) — very close to threshold
key_findings: Zero in-sample obligors had FCA settlements at or above $25M threshold in 2020-2024.

Erlanger Health is the strongest in-sample signal: DOJ-intervened FCA complaint filed July 2024 with estimated >$100M exposure, on top of prior $40M+CIA history from 2005. This is a high-quality CIA-recidivism signal even pre-settlement.
Zero blind obligors had FCA settlements at or above $25M threshold in 2015-2018.
ETMC at $21M (Aug 2018) is the closest below-threshold blind period case; if threshold were lowered to $20M it would fire.

Halifax Health's $85M Stark settlement was March 2014 - just 10 months before blind window start. A wider blind window (2014-2018) would catch this. This is the type of obligor the detector aims to flag pre-issuance.

Common allegation pattern: Stark Law / Anti-Kickback referral relationships dominate hospital FCA settlements. Wage index/cost report misreporting is secondary pattern (Yavapai, predecessors to Mosaic).

Detector signal observations: (1) The $25M threshold yields zero hits in both windows for these specific obligors, suggesting either (a) these obligor lists were ex-ante selected to avoid major FCA history, or (b) major FCA settlements concentrate in larger systems not in muni universe. (2) Erlanger Health's DOJ-intervention-without-settlement is potentially the strongest predictive signal in-sample.
Recommend the detector include DOJ-intervened FCA complaints (not just settlements) as a fire condition, with subordinate fire at $5M+ settlement combined with prior CIA breach.
